I’ll read the handoff, review, and notes alongside the research overview and progress files, then summarize what the new results establish and what remains open.

The main advance is that the recurrence now reaches the much smaller error scale needed by the broader program. The latest audit then budgets coefficient errors, rounding, and numerical integration at that scale. I’m checking the conditions carefully: the records distinguish these analytical guarantees from a certified working evaluator, which is still unfinished.

The research has turned the recurrence into **a controlled approximation hierarchy, with an explicit route toward evaluating it accurately**. The progress has four main parts.

1. **Each additional correction now has a quantified benefit.**  
   The opening recurrence work proved natural-scale error bounds of
   \[
   X^{-(p+3/4)}
   \]
   at each fixed correction order \(p\), with a matching Riemann–Siegel truncation. These bounds cover the field, its first three spatial derivatives, and its first time derivative on the stated complex neighborhoods. They extend across every fixed compact negative-time interval away from zero, with explicit dependence on the interval. This gives the hierarchy a mathematical payoff beyond organizing the formulas. [Overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/research-overview/01_RECURRENCE_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261026.md)

2. **The recurrence can reach the much smaller outer amplitude scale.**  
   Fixed-order bounds alone were insufficient after conversion to that scale. The subsequent work controlled the constants and tails while allowing the order to grow with height. With
   \[
   L=\log(X/(4\pi)),\qquad p=\lfloor L/2\rfloor,
   \]
   it obtains eventual error at most \(e^{-L^{2}/4}\), measured against the positive outer amplitude envelope, on \(1\le T\le2\), where the original heat time is \(-T\). This recovers the earlier outer-accuracy target through the systematic recurrence. Every arithmetic mode and the bounded Riemann–Siegel integral remain included. [Note 05](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/notes/05_CONTROLLED_ORDER_GROWTH_AUDIT_20261026.md)

3. **The retained integral now has a justified numerical integration prescription.**  
   This is a central new accomplishment of Note 06. A bound on an integral’s size does not establish how accurately a finite numerical rule approximates it. The research supplies the missing coefficient regularity and complex bounds, handles the apparent coefficient singularities analytically, and derives a rule requiring \(O(L^{2})\) nodes per branch, with at most two branches. It also accounts separately for errors in nodes, weights, and boundaries. [Note 06](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/notes/06_COEFFICIENT_ROUNDING_AND_RS_QUADRATURE_20261026.md)

4. **The desired accuracy now has a complete conditional evaluation budget.**  
   The latest audit allocates the total error among mathematical truncation, coefficient and phase inputs, normalization, integration, geometry, and arithmetic rounding. Under its stated contracts, sufficient requested input and arithmetic precision is
   \[
   \frac{3L^{2}}{8\log 2}+O(L\log L)\quad\text{bits}.
   \]
   That identifies how accurate the computational ingredients must be to preserve the outer-scale result. It is a sufficient specification; actual software precision and runtime still require certification. The full arithmetic sum also remains, so the modest quadrature count does not establish a similarly modest total runtime. [Assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/reviews/05_EVALUATION_ERROR_ASSESSMENT_20261026.md)

**The remaining gap is now more concrete:** construct and certify the routines supplying gamma values, logarithms, phases, normalization, integration nodes and weights, and cutoff decisions, then verify their errors against these budgets. That is why the bounded audit is complete while the broader evaluator task remains partial.

These results strengthen the negative-time approximation machinery. Transferring them to the physical observables, joining the time regimes, and establishing conclusions about zeros remain separate obligations. The recorded proofs have same-model internal assessments; independent specialist validation is still outstanding.
